Shipboard Girl

Roy Lichtenstein’s offset lithograph of a smiling blonde woman at a ship’s rail, in red, blue, and yellow dots and flat color with black key lines.

Source
V&A: Shipboard Girl, CIRC.649-1967
Creator
Roy Lichtenstein
Made
1965
Style
Pop art (agent-proposed, not yet reviewed by a person)
Moods
Bright, graphic, cheerful
Evidence
Downloaded and inspected the V&A image of its copy, CIRC.649-1967 (1400 × 1810 px), in a scratchpad. No image is stored.
Reviewed
28 September 2026
Rights
Link and metadata only. License: unverified. Rights policy

Context

The V&A records an offset lithograph on paper, sheet 69 × 51.5 cm, printed by Graphic Industries, Inc. and published by Leo Castelli, New York, 1965, signed “R Lichtenstein”. V&A.

Observed

  • The face and neck are covered in red dots on white; the hair is flat yellow with thick black strands.
  • Two blue dot fields fill the sky at the top and the area behind the shoulder.
  • A solid ultramarine block with white horizontal stripes sits at lower right.
  • The lips are flat red with a white highlight shape and a black outline.
  • A ship’s rail and a rope net are drawn in thick black lines over white.
  • The image is printed with a wide white margin. There are no speech balloons or words in the image.

Why it belongs

This print shows the balance of the idiom: roughly equal areas of dot tint, flat color, and white, held together by black.

The dots are large enough to see as dots at print size, which is the scale the style record asks for on screen.

Borrow

Use red dots for a warm tint and blue dots for a cool tint, and never mix them in one shape.

Leave generous white around a dense panel so that the dots do not fill the whole page.
